title: project-context
summary: Writes or checks the `.dlcontext.json` file beside a project: platform, config and define set, with the .dproj SHA-1 for staleness
intro: Read this when the language server or a tool must know which platform and configuration a project is built for without guessing. project-context resolves the .dproj (or, for a .dpr with no .dproj, the platform and config you pass) and writes the context file next to the project. --check writes nothing and exits 1 with the reason when the file is missing or stale.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint project-context --project <x.dproj|x.dpr> [--platform P] [--config C] [--output <file>] [--json] [--check] (writes <base>.dlcontext.json beside the project: platform, config and the complete effective define set, plus the .dproj SHA-1 for staleness; --check writes nothing and exits 1 saying why when the file is missing or stale; a .dpr with no .dproj exits 2 unless --platform and --config are both given)

questions.ask: Which platform and defines does this project build with?
Is the context file still current?
